```{r setup}
#| include: false
if (nzchar(params$pkg_path) && dir.exists(file.path(params$pkg_path, "R"))) {
  devtools::load_all(params$pkg_path, quiet = TRUE)
} else {
  library(stateELP)
}

spec <- read_el_spec(params$spec_file)

# Dev mode by default: the document runs the stage. `results_file` switches to
# RDS mode. Analysis logic lives in R/, never here: this file holds the prose,
# the captions, and one call per figure or table.
res <- if (!is.null(params$results_file) && nzchar(params$results_file)) {
  readRDS(params$results_file)
} else {
  # Prep 2 reads the roster and the ELP base table; the academic table is not used.
  bundle <- as_el_data(el_long_sim, roster = el_roster_sim, spec = spec)
  run_prep2(bundle, spec)
}

# Which slots came back. `h` is "has it", `n` is "is it missing": Quarto reads
# a second `!` inside `!expr` as a second YAML tag, so the negation is its own name.
slots <- c("counts_by_year", "el_share", "by_grade_span", "by_grade",
           "by_district", "district_bins", "entry_sources", "entry_grade",
           "entry_by_year", "entry_cohorts", "time_in_status", "initial_elp",
           "profile", "monitoring", "criteria_crosswalk")
h <- vapply(slots, function(s) !is.null(res[[s]]), TRUE)
n <- !h

lt_years <- res$meta$lt_el_years
min_cell <- res$meta$min_cell
latest <- res$meta$latest_year
```

## Sample

`r res$meta$sample`

`r if (res$meta$short_panel) "**Fewer than five years are available. Trends over time will be thin; treat the year-to-year views as provisional.**" else ""`
:::

## Looking at

Trends over time, grade-level distribution, district variation, entry-grade
patterns, and demographic profiles (home language, disability status,
alternate-assessment participation, and newcomer vs. long-term EL indicators
where the delivery carries them).

## Looking for

Two things, not one.

1. **The shape of the EL population in its own right.** Where EL students
   concentrate by grade and district, how large the long-term-EL share is,
   and how uneven entry patterns are. A reclassification policy technically
   applies to everyone but lands unevenly: some grades and districts will feel
   a threshold change far more than others, simply because that is where the
   EL students are.
2. **The compositional facts that shape the later stages.** Heavily K/1
   entry, cumulative attrition by grade, and a concentrated long-term-EL
   presence are what will later justify weighting certain grades' evidence
   more cautiously, and analyzing newly arrived and long-term ELs as separate
   groups rather than one pooled population.

## Data coverage

Counts come from the roster only (the base table has rows only where a test
happened; the roster is the counting frame). Everything counted here is built
on the **`r spec_headline_label(spec)`** --- the score this state reports as a
student's overall English language proficiency result. The "Annual
`r spec_headline_label(spec)`" column counts student-years with an annual-form
result; alternate-form takers are reported as a group and never banded,
because their levels are on a different scale.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-coverage
#| tbl-cap: !expr sprintf("Roster coverage by year. Cells under %d are suppressed.", min_cell)
ft_prep2_coverage(res)
```

## 4. Entry-grade patterns and candidate cohorts

Each student's entry into EL status is dated from the roster, using the first
of the fields in `spec$data$entry_sources` that is delivered and non-missing
(by default `LEP_PROGRAM_START_DATE`, `COHORT_START_YEAR`, `YEAR_IN_STATUS`,
then `ENTRY_GRADE`, which assumes one grade per year). A state's own count of
years in the program maps onto `YEAR_IN_STATUS` through
`spec$data$columns$roster`; whether that count codes a student's first year as
1 or as 0 is detected from entrants the panel observes, unless the spec says.
A delivered start date reads on the academic calendar (a September date
belongs to the next spring year) unless `spec$data$entry_date_rule` says
otherwise. With none of these fields, the panel itself dates entry only when
the student first turns `current` *after* the panel opens (a student in K in
the panel's first year is also taken as a K entrant that year). A student
already EL in the panel's first year with nothing delivered to date them has an
**unknown** entry: their time in status is a lower bound, and they are excluded
from the entry views and from any Check 1 cohort.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-entry-sources
#| tbl-cap: "How each ever-current student's entry year was resolved. Rows below the delivered fields are what the panel can do on its own."
#| eval: !expr h[["entry_sources"]]
ft_prep2_entry_sources(res)
```

```{r}
#| output: asis
#| eval: !expr h[["entry_sources"]]
cat(paste(res$meta$notes$entry, collapse = "\n\n"), "\n")
```

## 5. Time in status: new vs. long-term ELs

Years in status count from the entry year resolved in section 4, not from a
student's first appearance in the panel. A student whose entry is unknown
(already EL when the panel opened, nothing delivered to date them) has only a
lower bound: the years they have been observed as `current`. Such a student
counts as long-term once observed for `r if (is.null(lt_years)) "the long-term threshold of" else lt_years`+
years, and is otherwise carried as *unknown*, which is why the long-term share
is reported as a range (at least / at most). The two bounds meet once every
student's entry is dated.

Distributions only. Per the slide-38 guardrail, no mean or average time in
status is computed anywhere in this document: a mean of durations across
students who entered at different grades, and are censored at different
points, describes no one.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-time-year
#| tbl-cap: !expr sprintf("New and long-term ELs by year. Long-term = %s+ years in status [DERIVED -- VERIFY]. \"At least\" counts students dated or observed current for %s+ years; \"at most\" adds every student whose entry is unknown and could be. First-year shares count dated entries only.", lt_years, lt_years)
#| eval: !expr h[["time_in_status"]]
ft_prep2_time_by_year(res)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-time-grade
#| fig-cap: !expr sprintf("Years in EL status among current ELs, by grade, %d. Grey marks unknown entry, observed for fewer years than the long-term threshold.", latest)
#| eval: !expr h[["time_in_status"]]
plot_time_in_status(res$time_in_status)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-time-grade
#| tbl-cap: !expr sprintf("New and long-term shares by grade, %d. This is the table that tells you where a pooled all-EL analysis would mix two different populations.", latest)
#| eval: !expr h[["time_in_status"]]
ft_prep2_time_by_grade(res)
```

```{r}
cat("The spec carries no structured long-term definition (`policy$timelines$lt_el_years`), so time in status is not computed (`time_in_status` is `NULL`).\n")
```

## Interpreting

This step is not just a technical prerequisite for choosing analytic samples.
It is the interpretive backdrop for every Data Check that follows. A
grade-level finding, a district pattern, or a subgroup difference in Data
Checks 1--4 has to be read through what this step shows: is that grade,
district, or subgroup representative of the EL population, or an outlier
shaped by unusual entry timing, thin N, or a concentrated long-term-EL
presence? Skipped or skimmed, this step lets later results be taken at face
value when they actually reflect population idiosyncrasy rather than anything
about the exit threshold.

::: {.callout-warning appearance="default" icon=false}
## Resist the urge to average

Nothing above averages across groups, and nothing reports a mean time in
status. Grade, district, and duration groups are shown as distributions and
shares so that the concentration itself stays visible. Keep it that way in
the stages that follow.
:::

## Decide before moving on

```{r}
#| output: asis
cat(paste0("- ", res$analytic_sample_memo, collapse = "\n"), "\n")
```

::: {.callout-tip appearance="default" icon=false}
## Decide

- **Which cohorts and subgroups are large and stable enough to analyze reliably?** Is there a clean K-start cohort for Data Check 1 (observed at entry, not pandemic-distorted, N well above the suppression floor)?
- **Which grades, districts, or subgroups are most likely to be affected by any eventual policy change** and warrant closer attention throughout?
- **Where would a single pooled "all ELs together" analysis obscure more than it reveals?** Most notably: newly arrived vs. long-term ELs, and the grades where the long-term share is concentrated.
:::
